title.zh: 卷一百二十五 列傳第六十三: 文藝上 韓昉 蔡松年子:珪 吳激 馬定國 任詢 趙可 郭長倩 蕭永祺 胡礪 王競 楊伯仁 鄭子聃 党懷英
title.en: Volume 125 Biographies 63: Wen Yishang, Han Fang, Cai Songnian Son: Gui, Wu Ji, Ma Dingguo, Ren Xun, Zhao Ke, Guo Zhangqian, Xiao Yongqi, Hu Li, Wang Jing, Yang Boren, Zheng Zidan, Dang Huaiying

sentences.zh: 列傳第六十三 文藝上 ○韓昉 蔡松年子 珪 吳激 馬定國 任詢 趙可 郭長倩 蕭永祺 胡礪 王競 楊伯仁 鄭子聃 党懷英

translations.literal: Biography 63, Literary Arts (Part One): Han Fang; Cai Songnian's son Gui; Wu Ji; Ma Dingguo; Ren Xun; Zhao Ke; Guo Changqian; Xiao Yongqi; Hu Li; Wang Jing; Yang Boren; Zheng Zidan; Dang Huaiying.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 63 — Literary Arts (Part One): Han Fang; Cai Songnian and his son Gui; Wu Ji; Ma Dingguo; Ren Xun; Zhao Ke; Guo Changqian; Xiao Yongqi; Hu Li; Wang Jing; Yang Boren; Zheng Zidan; and Dang Huaiying.

sentences.zh: 金初未有文字。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jin there were no written records.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jin there was as yet no written language or formal documentation.

sentences.zh: 世祖以來，漸立條教。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Shizu, regulations and teachings were gradually established.
translations.idiomatic: From the reign of Shizu onward, statutes and institutional rules were introduced step by step.

sentences.zh: 太祖既興，得遼舊人用之，使介往復，其言已文。

translations.literal: After Taizu arose, he obtained former Liao personnel and employed them; envoys going back and forth, their speech was already refined.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu had risen to power, he recruited former Liao officials, and the language used in diplomatic exchange was already polished literary Chinese.

sentences.zh: 太宗繼統，乃行選舉之法，及伐宋，取汴經籍圖，宋士多歸之。

translations.literal: Taizong succeeded to the rule, then implemented the selection and recruitment method; when attacking Song he took Bian's classics, records, and maps, and many Song scholars came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong inherited the throne he instituted civil-service examinations; in the campaign against the Song he seized the libraries and maps of Bianjing, and many Song literati entered Jin service.

sentences.zh: 熙宗款謁先聖，北面如弟子禮。

translations.literal: Xizong reverently visited the ancient sage, facing north in the manner of a disciple's rite.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong paid ceremonious homage to Confucius, standing to the north as a student would.

sentences.zh: 世宗、章宗之世，儒風丕變，庠序日盛，士由科第位至宰輔者接踵。

translations.literal: In the eras of Shizong and Zhangzong, Confucian influence greatly changed; academies grew daily prosperous, and scholars reaching minister and chancellor through the examination system followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong and Zhangzong Confucian culture flourished anew, schools multiplied, and men who entered government through the examinations rose in steady succession to the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 當時儒者雖無專門名家之學，然而朝廷典策、鄰國書命，粲然有可觀者矣。

translations.literal: Although Confucian scholars of that time had no specialized school of famous masters, nevertheless the court's canonical documents and neighboring states' letters and mandates were brilliantly worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jin scholars of that period had no masters of a single scholastic tradition, court memorials and treaties with foreign states were nonetheless accomplished works of genuine merit.

sentences.zh: 金用武得國，無以異於遼，而一代製作，能自樹立唐、宋之間，有非遼世所及，以文而不以武也。

translations.literal: Jin used military force to obtain the state, no different from Liao, yet one generation's productions could establish itself between Tang and Song, possessing what the Liao age did not reach, by culture rather than by war.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin, like the Liao before them, had won an empire by arms, yet in the cultural institutions of their age they could stand among the Tang and Song in ways the Liao never had—because they ruled through letters as much as through the sword.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「言之不文，行之不遠。」

translations.literal: The "Zhuan" says: "If speech is not refined, practice will not reach far."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "What is not expressed in refined language will not carry far in practice."

sentences.zh: 文治有補於人之家國，豈一日之效哉。

translations.literal: Literary governance has benefit for people's families and states—how could it be the effect of a single day?
translations.idiomatic: Civil culture strengthens a household and a realm alike; its fruits are never the work of a single day.

sentences.zh: 作《文藝傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Treatise on Literary Arts" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the "Treatise on Literary Arts" was written.

sentences.zh: 韓昉，字公美，燕京人。

translations.literal: Han Fang, style name Gongmei, was a native of Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fang, whose style name was Gongmei, came from Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 仕遼，累世通顯。

translations.literal: He served Liao; for successive generations his family was prominent.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served the Liao for generations and held eminent rank.

sentences.zh: 昉五歲喪父，哭泣能盡哀。

translations.literal: Fang at five years lost his father; in weeping he could exhaust his grief.
translations.idiomatic: Fang lost his father at the age of five and wept with the full depth of filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 天慶二年，中進士第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqing he placed first among jinshi graduates.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tianqing reign he took first place in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 補右拾遺，轉史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Reminder, then transferred to Historiographical Institute Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Reminder and later became a compiler at the Historiographical Institute.

sentences.zh: 累遷少府少監、乾文閣待制。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Vice Director of the Palace Storehouse and Awaiting Draftsman at the Qianwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Palace Storehouse and awaiting draftsman at the Qianwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 加衛尉卿，知制誥，充高麗國信使。

translations.literal: He was added as Commandant of the Guards, knew imperial rescripts, and served as envoy bearing credentials to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commandant of the Guards and charged with drafting imperial rescripts, then sent as credentialed envoy to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 高麗雖舊通好，天會四年，奉表稱籓而不肯進誓表，累使要約，皆不得要領。

translations.literal: Although Goryeo had long been on friendly terms, in the fourth year of Tianhui it presented a memorial declaring vassalage but refused to submit a sworn covenant; repeatedly envoys pressed for agreement, yet none obtained the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo had long maintained friendly relations with the court, but in the fourth year of Tianhui it sent a memorial acknowledging vassalage while refusing to submit a sworn covenant; repeated missions pressed for terms, yet none could secure a definitive agreement.

sentences.zh: 而昉複至高麗，移督再三。

translations.literal: Fang again went to Goryeo, sending repeated letters of urging.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was sent to Goryeo again and pressed his demands in letter after letter.

sentences.zh: 高麗征國中讀書知古今者，商榷辭旨，使酬答專對。

translations.literal: Goryeo summoned within the state those who read books and knew past and present, to discuss wording and intent, and had them reply in specialized responses.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo gathered its most learned men to deliberate on every phrase and appointed them to answer Fang point by point.

sentences.zh: 凡涉旬乃始置對，謂昉曰：「小國事遼、宋二百年無誓表，未嘗失籓臣禮。

translations.literal: Only after more than ten days did they begin to set forth replies, saying to Fang: "Our small state served Liao and Song for two hundred years without a sworn covenant and never failed in the rites of a vassal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Only after ten days did they begin to reply, telling Fang: "For two hundred years our small kingdom served Liao and Song without a sworn covenant and never once failed in the duties of a vassal.

sentences.zh: 今事上國，當與事遼、宋同禮。

translations.literal: Now in serving the superior state, we ought to follow the same rites as in serving Liao and Song.
translations.idiomatic: In serving your great state we should observe the same ceremonial terms we kept with Liao and Song.

sentences.zh: 而屢盟長亂，聖人所不與，必不敢用誓表。」

translations.literal: Yet repeated covenants prolong disorder; the sages do not approve of them—we absolutely dare not use a sworn covenant."
translations.idiomatic: Repeated treaties only breed long disorder, and the sages would not approve—we cannot possibly adopt a sworn covenant."

sentences.zh: 昉曰：「貴國必欲用古禮，舜五載一巡狩，群後四朝。

translations.literal: Fang said: "If your honorable state must use ancient rites, Shun every five years made one inspection tour, and the feudal lords attended court four times.
translations.idiomatic: Fang replied: "If your state insists on ancient precedent, recall that Shun made a tour of inspection every five years and the feudal lords attended court four times in each cycle.

sentences.zh: 週六年五服一朝，又六年王乃時巡，諸侯各朝于方嶽。

translations.literal: In Zhou, within six years the five domains attended court once; after another six years the king then made seasonal tours, and the feudal lords each attended at the directional peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou, the five domains came to court once every six years; after another six years the king toured the realm, and each lord attended at his assigned mountain altar.

sentences.zh: 今天子方事西狩，則貴國當從朝會矣。」

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is just undertaking a western hunt—then your honorable state ought to follow the court assembly."
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is presently engaged in a western hunt—so your state should come to the court assembly at once."

sentences.zh: 高麗人無以對，乃曰：「徐議之。」

translations.literal: The Goryeo people had nothing to reply and then said: "Let us discuss it slowly."
translations.idiomatic: The Goryeo envoys had no answer and said only, "We must deliberate further."

sentences.zh: 昉曰：「誓表朝會，一言決耳。」

translations.literal: Fang said: "Sworn covenant or court assembly—settled in a single word."
translations.idiomatic: Fang said: "The sworn covenant or the court assembly—let one word decide it."

sentences.zh: 於是高麗乃進誓表如約，昉乃還。

translations.literal: Thereupon Goryeo then submitted the sworn covenant as agreed, and Fang returned.
translations.idiomatic: At that Goryeo submitted the sworn covenant as required, and Fang returned home.

sentences.zh: 宗幹大說曰：「非卿誰能辦此。」

translations.literal: Zonggan was greatly pleased and said: "If not you, who could accomplish this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zonggan was delighted and said, "Who but you could have brought this off?"

sentences.zh: 因謂執事者曰：「自今出疆之使，皆宜擇人。」

translations.literal: He then said to those in charge: "From now on envoys crossing the border ought all to be carefully chosen."
translations.idiomatic: He then told the officials in charge, "From now on every envoy sent abroad must be chosen with care."

sentences.zh: 明年，加昭文館直學士，兼堂後官。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Direct Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, concurrently holding a post in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed direct academician of the Zhaowen Hall and also given a concurrent post in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 再加諫議大夫，遷翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was further made Remonstrance Censor, then transferred to Hanlin Attendant Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Remonstrance Censor and then to Hanlin attendant lecturer.

sentences.zh: 改禮部尚書，遷翰林學士，兼太常卿、修國史，尚書如故。

translations.literal: He was changed to Minister of Rites, transferred to Hanlin Academician, concurrently Grand Master of Ceremonies and compiler of national history, his ministry post remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Rites and Hanlin academician, while retaining his ministry rank and concurrently serving as Grand Master of Ceremonies and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 昉自天會十二年入禮部，在職凡七年。

translations.literal: Fang from the twelfth year of Tianhui entered the Ministry of Rites; in office altogether seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Fang entered the Ministry of Rites in the twelfth year of Tianhui and held office there for seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 當是時，朝廷方議禮，制度或因或革，故昉在禮部兼太常甚久雲。

translations.literal: At that time the court was just discussing rites; institutions were sometimes retained and sometimes reformed—thus Fang in the Ministry of Rites concurrently holding Grand Master of Ceremonies was very long, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then debating ritual reform, adopting or revising institutions as needed—hence Fang's long tenure in the Ministry of Rites with concurrent charge of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 除濟南尹，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Jinan and invested as Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jinan and appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，表乞致仕，不許。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong he memorialized requesting retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong he petitioned to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 六年，再表乞致仕，乃除汴京留守，封鄆國公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again memorialized requesting retirement; then he was appointed Bianjing garrison commander and enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he petitioned again to retire and was appointed garrison commander of Bianjing and enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 複請如初，以儀同三司致仕。

translations.literal: He again requested as at first and retired with the rank of Pillar of the State, Third Class.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned once more as before and was permitted to retire with the honorary rank of Pillar of the State, Third Class.

sentences.zh: 天德初，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was added Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells, Third Class.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiande era he was given the additional rank of Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells, Third Class.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He passed away.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 年六十八。

translations.literal: His age was sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 昉性仁厚，待物甚寬。

translations.literal: Fang's nature was benevolent and generous; in treating things he was very lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was by nature kind and magnanimous and treated others with exceptional forbearance.

sentences.zh: 有家奴誣告昉以馬資送叛人出境，考之無狀，有司以奴還昉，昉待之如初，曰：「奴誣主人以罪，求為良耳，何足怪哉。」

translations.literal: A household slave falsely accused Fang of using horse funds to send rebels across the border; investigation found no basis; the authorities returned the slave to Fang, and Fang treated him as at first, saying: "The slave falsely accused the master of a crime, seeking to become a commoner—that is all; what is there to find strange?"
translations.idiomatic: A household slave falsely accused him of using government horse funds to help rebels escape across the border; the investigation found no evidence, and the authorities returned the slave to Fang, who treated him exactly as before, saying, "The man accused his master in hope of becoming a free commoner—there is nothing remarkable in that."

sentences.zh: 人稱其長者。

translations.literal: People called him a man of mature virtue.
translations.idiomatic: People praised him as a man of true magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 昉雖貴，讀書未嘗去手，善屬文，最長於詔冊，作《太祖睿德神功碑》，當世稱之。

translations.literal: Although Fang was noble in rank, in reading books he never left them from his hand; he was skilled at composing prose and was best at edicts and patent letters; he composed the "Stele of Taizu's Sagacious Virtue and Divine Merit," and his contemporaries praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose to high office, Fang never set his books aside; he was an accomplished writer, especially famed for edicts and patent letters, and his "Stele of Taizu's Sagacious Virtue and Divine Merit" was acclaimed in his own day.

sentences.zh: 自使高麗歸，後高麗使者至，必問昉安否雲。

translations.literal: From the time he returned as envoy from Goryeo, afterward when Goryeo envoys arrived they invariably inquired whether Fang was well, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: After his mission to Goryeo, every subsequent Goryeo envoy to the court asked after his health.

sentences.zh: 蔡松年

translations.literal: Cai Songnian.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Songnian.

sentences.zh: 蔡松年，字伯堅。

translations.literal: Cai Songnian, style name Bojian.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Songnian, whose style name was Bojian,

sentences.zh: 父靖，宋宣和末，守燕山。

translations.literal: His father Jing, at the end of Song Xuanhe, guarded Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: was the son of Jing, who at the end of the Xuanhe reign held Yanshan for the Song.

sentences.zh: 松年從父來，管勾機宜文字。

translations.literal: Songnian followed his father and served as overseer of opportune documentary matters.
translations.idiomatic: Songnian followed his father and served as overseer of military correspondence.

sentences.zh: 宗望軍至白河，郭藥師敗，靖以燕山府降，元帥府辟松年為令史。

translations.literal: Zongwang's army reached the White River; Guo Yaoshi was defeated; Jing surrendered the Yanshan prefecture; the Marshal's Headquarters recruited Songnian as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang's army reached the White River and Guo Yaoshi was defeated, Jing surrendered the Yanshan prefecture, and the marshal's headquarters appointed Songnian as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 天會中，遼、宋舊有官者皆換授，松年為太子中允，除真定府判官，自此為真定人。

translations.literal: During Tianhui, former Liao and Song officials were all given exchanged appointments; Songnian became Palace Attendant; he was appointed administrative aide of Zhending Prefecture—from then on he was counted as a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhui era former Liao and Song officials were reappointed to Jin posts; Songnian became a palace attendant and was made administrative aide of Zhending Prefecture, thereafter regarded as a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 嘗從元帥府與齊俱伐宋。

translations.literal: He once followed the Marshal's Headquarters together with Qi in attacking Song.
translations.idiomatic: He once accompanied the marshal's headquarters on a joint campaign with Qi against the Song.

sentences.zh: 是時，初平真定西山群盜，山中居民為賊汙者千餘家，松年力為辨論，竟得不坐。

translations.literal: At that time they had just pacified the bandit gangs of western Zhending mountains; mountain residents tainted by bandits numbered more than a thousand households; Songnian vigorously argued on their behalf, and in the end they were not punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit gangs of the western Zhending hills were newly suppressed, more than a thousand mountain households were implicated as collaborators; Songnian argued strenuously in their defense, and they were ultimately not punished.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，置行台尚書省於汴，松年為行台刑部郎中，都元帥宗弼領行台事，伐宋，松年兼總軍中六部事。

translations.literal: The Qi state was abolished; the Branch Secretariat was established at Bian; Songnian was Branch Secretariat Director of the Ministry of Punishments; Grand Marshal Zongbi led Branch Secretariat affairs; attacking Song, Songnian concurrently oversaw the six ministries' affairs in the army.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qi state was abolished a branch secretariat was set up at Bianjing; Songnian became director in the Ministry of Punishments on the branch staff; when Grand Marshal Zongbi led the branch secretariat on campaign against the Song, Songnian concurrently oversaw the six ministries within the army.

sentences.zh: 宋稱臣，師還，宗弼入為左丞相，薦松年為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Song declared itself a vassal; the army returned; Zongbi entered office as Left Chancellor and recommended Songnian as Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song submitted as a vassal and the army withdrew, Zongbi entered the capital as left chancellor and recommended Songnian as vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 皇統七年，尚書省令史許霖告田玨黨事，松年素與玨不相能。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huangtong, Secretariat clerk Xu Lin reported Tian Jue's factional affair; Songnian had long been incompatible with Jue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Huangtong, secretariat clerk Xu Lin denounced Tian Jue for factional intrigue; Songnian had long been at odds with Jue.

sentences.zh: 是時宗弼當國，玨性剛正，好評論人物，其党皆君子，韓企先為相愛重之。

translations.literal: At that time Zongbi held state power; Jue's nature was upright and firm, fond of commenting on people's characters; his faction were all gentlemen; Han Qixian as chancellor cherished and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi then dominated the government; Jue was upright and outspoken, given to judging men's character, and his associates were men of integrity whom Chancellor Han Qixian favored.

sentences.zh: 而松年、許霖、曹望之欲與玨相結，玨拒之，由是構怨。

translations.literal: But Songnian, Xu Lin, and Cao Wangzhi wished to ally with Jue; Jue refused them—thereby enmity was formed.
translations.idiomatic: Songnian, Xu Lin, and Cao Wangzhi sought an alliance with Jue, but he rebuffed them, and from that enmity arose.

sentences.zh: 故松年、許霖構成玨等罪狀，勸宗弼誅之，君子之党熄焉。

translations.literal: Therefore Songnian and Xu Lin fabricated Jue and others' criminal charges, urging Zongbi to execute them—the party of gentlemen was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Songnian and Xu Lin then fabricated charges against Jue and his circle and urged Zongbi to put them to death, and the party of upright men was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，松年遷左司員外郎。

translations.literal: That year Songnian was transferred to Vice Director of the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: That year Songnian was promoted to vice director of the left bureau.

sentences.zh: 松年前在宗弼府，而海陵以宗室子在宗弼軍中任使，用是相厚善。

translations.literal: Songnian had earlier been in Zongbi's headquarters, while Hailing as an imperial clansman served in assignments in Zongbi's army—by this they were mutually close and friendly.
translations.idiomatic: Songnian had earlier served in Zongbi's headquarters, where Hailing, then a young imperial clansman on assignment in Zongbi's army, became his close friend.

sentences.zh: 天德初，擢吏部侍郎，俄遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was promoted Vice Minister of Personnel, and soon transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiande era he was promoted to vice minister of personnel and soon thereafter to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 海陵遷中都，徙榷貨物以實都城，複鈔引法，皆自松年啟之。

translations.literal: Hailing moved the capital to Zhongdu, transferred monopoly goods to enrich the capital city, and restored the paper-note tally system—all initiated from Songnian.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing moved the capital to Zhongdu, Songnian proposed transferring state monopoly goods to stock the new city and reviving the paper-note tally system.

sentences.zh: 海陵謀伐宋，以松年家世仕宋，故亟擢顯位以聳南人觀聽，遂以松年為賀宋正旦使，使還改吏部尚書，尋拜參知政一。

translations.literal: Hailing plotted to attack Song; because Songnian's family for generations had served Song, he therefore quickly promoted him to conspicuous rank to startle southern people's sight and hearing; then he made Songnian envoy congratulating Song on New Year's Day; on return from the mission he was changed to Minister of Personnel, and soon invested Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: As Hailing planned war against the Song, he rapidly promoted Songnian—whose family had long served the Song—to a conspicuous post so as to impress the south, then sent him as New Year's envoy to the Song; on his return he was made minister of personnel and soon appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 是年，自崇德大夫進銀青光祿大夫，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: That year, from Grand Master of Cherished Virtue he advanced to Grand Master with Silver-Gleaming Light, and was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was advanced from Grand Master of Cherished Virtue to Grand Master with Silver-Gleaming Light and appointed right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為左丞，封郜國公。

translations.literal: Before long he became Left Vice Director and was enfeoffed as Duke of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became left vice director and was enfeoffed as Duke of Gao.

sentences.zh: 初，海陵愛宋使人山呼聲，使神衛軍習之。

translations.literal: At first Hailing loved the Song envoys' mountain-shouting cry and had the Divine Guard Army practice it.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had taken a liking to the ceremonial shout with which Song envoys hailed the throne and ordered the Divine Guard to practice it.

sentences.zh: 及孫道夫賀正隆三年正旦，入見，山呼聲不類往年來者。

translations.literal: When Sun Daofu came to congratulate on the New Year of the third year of Zhenglong, on entering audience the mountain-shouting cry was not like those of previous years.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Daofu came to offer New Year's congratulations in the third year of Zhenglong, his ceremonial shout on entering audience differed from that of earlier envoys.

sentences.zh: 道夫退，海陵謂宰臣曰：「宋人知我使神衛軍習其聲，此必蔡松年、胡礪泄之。」

translations.literal: Daofu withdrew; Hailing said to the chief ministers: "The Song people know we had the Divine Guard practice their cry—this must have been leaked by Cai Songnian and Hu Li."
translations.idiomatic: After Daofu withdrew, Hailing told his chief ministers, "The Song must know we had the Divine Guard practice their shout—Songnian and Hu Li must have leaked it."

sentences.zh: 松年惶恐對曰：「臣若懷此心，便當族滅。」

translations.literal: Songnian in fear replied: "If your servant harbored such a heart, let his clan be exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: Songnian answered in alarm, "If I harbored such intent, let my entire clan be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 久之，進拜右丞相，加儀同三司，封衛國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Right Grand Councilor, granted the rank of Pillar of the State, Third Class, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to right grand councilor, granted the rank of Pillar of the State, Third Class, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 正隆四年薨，年五十三。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhenglong, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhenglong at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 海陵悼惜之，奠於其第，命作祭文以見意。

translations.literal: Hailing mourned and regretted it, offered sacrifices at his residence, and ordered a funeral elegy written to express his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing mourned him deeply, offered sacrifices at his residence, and ordered a funeral elegy written to express his grief.

sentences.zh: 加封吳國公，諡文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously advanced to Duke of Wu and given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously advanced to Duke of Wu and given the posthumous title Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 起複其子三河主簿珪為翰林修撰，璋賜進士第。

translations.literal: His son Gui, recorder of Sanhe, was recalled from mourning and made Hanlin Compiler; Zhang was granted the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui, recorder of Sanhe, was recalled from mourning and appointed Hanlin compiler, and Zhang was granted the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 遣翰林待制蕭籲護送其喪，歸葬真定，四品以下官離都城十里送之，道路之費，皆從官給。

translations.literal: Hanlin Awaiting Draftsman Xiao Yu was sent to escort the funeral procession; he was buried at Zhending; officials of the fourth rank and below escorted him ten li from the capital; travel expenses were all paid from official funds.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin awaiting draftsman Xiao Yu was sent to escort the funeral; Songnian was buried at Zhending, with officials of the fourth rank and below seeing him off ten li from the capital while travel expenses were paid from official funds.

sentences.zh: 松年事繼母以孝聞，喜周恤親黨，性複豪侈，不計家之有無。

translations.literal: Songnian served his stepmother with filial piety renowned; he delighted in generously relieving kin and clansmen; his nature was again extravagant, not calculating the household's having or not having.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for filial devotion to his stepmother and for generous support of kin and friends; he was by nature lavish and gave no thought to his household's means.

sentences.zh: 文詞清麗，尤工樂府，與吳激齊名，時號「吳蔡體。」

translations.literal: His literary words were clear and beautiful; he was especially skilled at yuefu; with Wu Ji he shared equal fame, and the age called it the "Wu-Cai style."
translations.idiomatic: His verse was refined and elegant, especially in yuefu poetry; he and Wu Ji were equally famed, and contemporaries spoke of the "Wu-Cai style."

sentences.zh: 有集行於世。

translations.literal: A collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of his writings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子珪。

translations.literal: His son was Gui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gui.

sentences.zh: 子 珪

translations.literal: Son: Gui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui.

sentences.zh: 珪字正甫。

translations.literal: Gui's style name was Zhengfu.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, whose style name was Zhengfu,

sentences.zh: 中進士第，不求調，久乃除澄州軍事判官，遷三河主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination but did not seek appointment; only after a long time was he appointed military administrative aide of Cheng Prefecture, then transferred to registrar of Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: passed the jinshi examination but declined to seek a post; only after a long interval was he appointed military administrative aide of Cheng Prefecture, later becoming registrar of Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複翰林修撰，同知制誥。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his father, he was recalled to Hanlin Compiler, concurrently knowing imperial rescripts.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was recalled to serve as Hanlin compiler and deputy drafter of imperial rescripts.

sentences.zh: 在職八年，改戶部員外郎，兼太常丞。

translations.literal: In office eight years, he was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, concurrently Vice Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in office he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently vice director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 珪號為辨博，凡朝廷制度損益，珪為編類詳定檢討刪定官。

translations.literal: Gui was known as discriminating and broad in learning; for all court institutions' additions and subtractions, Gui served as compiler-classifying, detailed fixing, examining, and revising officer.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was known for erudition and precision; whenever court institutions were revised, he served on the committee for compilation, detailed review, and final revision.

sentences.zh: 初，兩燕王墓舊在中都東城外，海陵廣京城圍，墓在東城內。

translations.literal: At first the two Yan-king tombs were formerly east outside Zhongdu's city wall; Hailing expanded the capital's wall circuit, and the tombs lay within the eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: The two tombs of the Yan kings had originally lain east of Zhongdu outside the walls; when Hailing enlarged the capital, they fell inside the eastern quarter of the city.

sentences.zh: 前嘗有盜發其墓，大定九年詔改葬於城外。

translations.literal: Previously robbers had opened the tombs; in the ninth year of Dading an edict ordered reburial outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Grave robbers had once opened them, and in the ninth year of Dading an edict ordered them reburied outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 俗傳六國時燕王及太子丹之葬，及啟壙，其東墓之柩題其和曰「燕靈王舊。」

translations.literal: Popular tradition said they were the burials of the Yan king and Crown Prince Dan of the Six States period; when the vault was opened, on the eastern tomb's coffin the inscription on its cover read "Yan Ling Wang jiu."
translations.idiomatic: Popular tradition held that they were the tombs of the Yan king and Crown Prince Dan of the Warring States period; when the vault was opened, the eastern coffin bore on its lid the inscription "Yan Ling Wang jiu."

sentences.zh: 「舊」，古「柩」字，通用。

translations.literal: Jiu" is the ancient character for "coffin," used interchangeably.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu" was the archaic form of the character for "coffin," used interchangeably in such inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 乃西漢高祖子劉建葬也。

translations.literal: It was in fact the burial of Liu Jian, son of Western Han's Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb was in fact that of Liu Jian, son of Emperor Gaozu of the Western Han.

sentences.zh: 其西墓，蓋燕康王劉嘉之葬也。

translations.literal: The western tomb was probably the burial of Yan King Kang, Liu Jia.
translations.idiomatic: The western tomb was evidently that of Liu Jia, King Kang of Yan.

sentences.zh: 珪作《兩燕王墓辯》，據葬制名物款刻甚詳。

translations.literal: Gui composed "A Disputation on the Two Yan-King Tombs," relying on burial regulations, named objects, and inscriptions in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Gui wrote "A Disputation on the Two Yan-King Tombs," drawing in meticulous detail on burial regulations, ritual objects, and the tomb inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 安國軍節度判官高元鼎坐監臨奸事，求援于太常博士田居實、大理司直吳長行、吏部主事高震亨、大理評事王元忠。

translations.literal: Anguo Army military commissioner administrative aide Gao Yuanding sat guilty of supervising licentious affairs and sought aid from Grand Master of Ceremonies academician Tian Jushi, Court of Judicial Review investigating officer Wu Changxing, Ministry of Personnel principal clerk Gao Zhenheng, and Court of Judicial Review judging officer Wang Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanding, administrative aide to the military commissioner of the Anguo army, was charged with condoning sexual misconduct and sought help from Tian Jushi, an academician of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, Wu Changxing, an investigating officer of the Court of Judicial Review, Gao Zhenheng, a principal clerk of the Ministry of Personnel, and Wang Yuanzhong, a judging officer of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 震亨以屬鞫問官禦史台典事李仲柔，仲柔發之。

translations.literal: Zhenheng entrusted it to investigating officer Censorate clerk Li Zhongrou; Zhongrou exposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenheng passed the matter to Li Zhongrou, a clerk of the Censorate charged with investigation, and Zhongrou exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 珪與刑部員外郎王翛、宛平主簿任詢、前衛州防禦判官閻恕、承事郎高複亨、文林郎翟詢、敦武校尉王景晞、進義校尉任師望，坐與居實等轉相傳教，或令元鼎逃避，居實、長行、震亨、元忠各杖八十，翛、珪、詢、恕、複亨、霍詢各笞四十，景晞、師望各徒二年，官贖外並的決。

translations.literal: Gui together with Ministry of Punishments Vice Director Wang Xiao, Wanping registrar Ren Xun, former Weizhou defense administrative aide Yan Shu, Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement Gao Fuheng, Literary Grove Gentleman Zhai Xun, Dunwu Commandant Wang Jingxi, and Jinyi Commandant Ren Shiwang sat guilty of mutually transmitting teachings with Jushi and others, or causing Yuanding to evade punishment; Jushi, Changxing, Zhenheng, and Yuanzhong each received eighty blows with the staff; Xiao, Gui, Xun, Shu, Fuheng, and Huo Xun each forty blows with the bamboo; Jingxi and Shiwang each penal servitude two years; beyond official redemption all were summarily executed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, together with Wang Xiao, vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, Ren Xun, registrar of Wanping, Yan Shu, former administrative aide of the Weizhou defense command, Gao Fuheng, gentleman for meritorious achievement, Zhai Xun, literary grove gentleman, Wang Jingxi, dunwu commandant, and Ren Shiwang, jinyi commandant, were convicted of passing messages among Jushi's circle or helping Yuanding evade prosecution; Jushi, Changxing, Zhenheng, and Yuanzhong were each sentenced to eighty strokes of the staff; Xiao, Gui, Xun, Shu, Fuheng, and Huo Xun to forty strokes of the bamboo; Jingxi and Shiwang to two years' penal servitude; and beyond whatever redemption their offices allowed, all punishments were carried out on the spot.

sentences.zh: 久之，除河東北路轉運副使，複入為修撰，遷禮部郎中，封真定縣男。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Vice Transport Commissioner of Hedong North Circuit, again entered as compiler, transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites, and enfeoffed as Baron of Zhending County.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed vice transport commissioner of the Hedong North circuit, recalled as a Hanlin compiler, promoted to director of the Ministry of Rites, and enfeoffed as Baron of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 珪已得風疾，失音不能言，乃除濰州刺史，同輩已奏謝，珪獨不能入見。

translations.literal: Gui had already contracted wind affliction, lost his voice and could not speak; then he was appointed Prefect of Weizhou; his peers had already presented thanks for appointment, but Gui alone could not enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had already been stricken with apoplexy and had lost his power of speech; he was nevertheless appointed prefect of Weizhou, and while his colleagues had already presented their thanks for appointment, Gui alone could not appear at court.

sentences.zh: 世宗以讓右丞唐括安禮、參政王蔚曰：「卿等閱書史，亦有不能言之人可以從政者乎。」

translations.literal: Shizong reproached Right Vice Director Tangutuo Anli and Vice Grand Councilor Wang Wei, saying: "You have read books and histories—is there also among those who cannot speak anyone who can engage in government?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizong rebuked right vice director Tangutuo Anli and vice grand councilor Wang Wei, saying, "You have read history—can a man who cannot speak truly hold office?"

sentences.zh: 又謂中丞劉仲誨曰：「蔡珪風疾不能奏謝，卿等何不糾之。

translations.literal: He further said to Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhonghui: "Cai Gui's wind affliction prevents him from presenting thanks for appointment—why do you not impeach him?
translations.idiomatic: He then said to censor-in-chief Liu Zhonghui, "Cai Gui's apoplexy kept him from presenting thanks for his appointment—why did you not impeach him?

sentences.zh: 人言卿等相為黨蔽，今果然邪？」

translations.literal: People say you mutually shield one another in factional cover—now is it really so?"
translations.idiomatic: People say you shield one another as a faction—is that not plainly true?"

sentences.zh: 珪乃致仕。

translations.literal: Gui then retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Gui thereupon retired from office.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 珪之文有《補正水經》五篇，合沈約、蕭子顯、魏收宋、齊、北魏志作《南北史志》三十卷，《續金石遺文跋尾》十卷，《晉陽志》十二卷，《文集》五十五卷。

translations.literal: Gui's writings included five chapters of "Correcting the Water Classic," combining Shen Yue's, Xiao Zixian's, and Wei Shou's Song, Qi, and Northern Wei gazetteers to make "North-South History Gazetteer" in thirty chapters, "Continued Colophons to Lost Bronze and Stone Inscriptions" in ten chapters, "Jinyang Gazetteer" in twelve chapters, and "Collected Works" in fifty-five chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Among Gui's writings were five chapters of "Correcting the Water Classic"; a thirty-chapter "North-South History Gazetteer" compiled from the Song, Qi, and Northern Wei gazetteers of Shen Yue, Xiao Zixian, and Wei Shou; ten chapters of "Continued Colophons to Lost Bronze and Stone Inscriptions"; twelve chapters of the "Jinyang Gazetteer"; and fifty-five chapters of collected works.

sentences.zh: 《補正水經》、《晉陽志》、《文集》今存，餘皆亡。

translations.literal: "Correcting the Water Classic," "Jinyang Gazetteer," and "Collected Works" exist today; the rest are all lost.
translations.idiomatic: The "Correcting the Water Classic," the "Jinyang Gazetteer," and the collected works survive today; all his other works are lost.

sentences.zh: 吳激，字彥高，建州人。

translations.literal: Wu Ji, style name Yangao, was a native of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ji, whose style name was Yangao, came from Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 父拭，宋進士，官終朝奉郎、知蘇州。

translations.literal: His father Shi was a Song jinshi; his final office was Gentleman for Court Attendance and prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi was a Song jinshi who ended his career as Gentleman for Court Attendance and prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 激，米芾之婿也。

translations.literal: Ji was Mi Fu's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was the son-in-law of the calligrapher Mi Fu.

sentences.zh: 工詩能文，字畫俊逸，得芾筆意。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry and able in prose; his calligraphy and painting were handsome and free, obtaining Fu's brush intent.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in poetry and prose, and his calligraphy and painting were elegant and spirited, capturing Mi Fu's brush manner.

sentences.zh: 尤精樂府，造語清婉，哀而不傷。

translations.literal: He was especially refined in yuefu; his phrasing was clear and gentle, mournful yet not wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially accomplished in yuefu poetry, with diction clear and delicate—lament without excess.

sentences.zh: 將宋命至金，以知名留不遣，命為翰林待制。

translations.literal: About to carry Song orders to Jin, because of his fame he was detained and not sent back; he was appointed Hanlin Awaiting Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to deliver a Song mission to the Jin, his fame led the court to detain him and appoint him Hanlin awaiting draftsman.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，出知深州，到官三日卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong he went out as prefect of Shenzhou; three days after reaching his post he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangtong he was sent out as prefect of Shenzhou and died three days after taking office.

sentences.zh: 詔賜其子錢百萬、粟三百斛、田三頃以周其家。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed on his son a million in cash, three hundred hu of grain, and three qing of fields to support his household.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted his son a million in cash, three hundred hu of grain, and three qing of land to support the family.

sentences.zh: 有《東山集》十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had "Eastern Mountain Collection" in ten chapters circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His "Eastern Mountain Collection" in ten chapters circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 「東山」，其自號也。

translations.literal: "Eastern Mountain" was his self-adopted style.
translations.idiomatic: "Eastern Mountain" was his chosen sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 馬定國

translations.literal: Ma Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 馬定國字子卿，茌平人。

translations.literal: Ma Dingguo, style name Ziqing, was a native of Chiping.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dingguo, whose style name was Ziqing, came from Chiping.

sentences.zh: 自少志趣不群。

translations.literal: From youth his aspirations were not of the common sort.
translations.idiomatic: From youth his temperament and ambitions set him apart from others.

sentences.zh: 宣、政未末題詩酒家壁，坐譏訕得罪，亦因以知名。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe and Zhenghe he inscribed a poem on a wine-shop wall, sat guilty of satirical mockery and offense, yet also thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xuanhe and Zhenghe reigns he wrote a poem on a tavern wall, was punished for satirical mockery, and thereby became famous.

sentences.zh: 阜昌初，遊歷下，以詩撼齊王豫，豫大悅，授監察禦史，仕至翰林學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Fuchang he traveled to Lixia, using a poem to stir Prince of Qi Yu; Yu was greatly pleased and appointed him Investigating Censor; he served up to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Fuchang era he traveled to Lixia and impressed Prince Yu of Qi with a poem; Yu was delighted and made him investigating censor, and he rose to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 《石鼓》自唐以來無定論，定國以字畫考之，雲是宇文周時所造，作辯萬餘言，出入傳記，引據甚明，學者以比蔡正甫《燕王墓辯》。

translations.literal: The "Stone Drums" since Tang had no settled conclusion; Dingguo examined them through characters and brushwork, saying they were made in the Yuwen Zhou period; he composed a disputation of more than ten thousand words, entering and exiting transmitted records, citations very clear—scholars compared it to Cai Zhengfu's "Disputation on the Yan-King Tombs."
translations.idiomatic: The "Stone Drums" had been disputed since the Tang; Dingguo studied their script and argued that they dated from the Northern Zhou of the Yuwen clan, writing a disputation of more than ten thousand words with clear citations from historical records—scholars compared it to Cai Zhengfu's "Disputation on the Yan-King Tombs."

sentences.zh: 初，學詩未有入處，夢其父與方寸白筆，從是文章大進。

translations.literal: At first in studying poetry he had not yet found entry; he dreamed his father gave him a square-inch white brush—from then his literary compositions greatly advanced.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still struggling to master poetry, he dreamed that his father gave him a small white brush, and from that time his writing advanced greatly.

sentences.zh: 有集傳於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of his writings circulated.

sentences.zh: 任詢，字君謨，易州軍市人。

translations.literal: Ren Xun, style name Junmo, was a native of Yizhou Junshi.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xun, whose style name was Junmo, came from Junshi in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 父貴，有才幹，善畫，喜談兵，宣、政間游江、浙。

translations.literal: His father Gui had talent and ability, was skilled at painting, delighted in discussing military affairs, and during Xuanhe and Zhenghe traveled Jiang and Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui was capable and skilled in painting, fond of military discussion, and during the Xuanhe and Zhenghe reigns traveled through Jiangnan and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 詢生於虔州，為人慷慨多大節。

translations.literal: Xun was born in Qianzhou; as a man he was magnanimous and possessed great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was born in Qianzhou and was by nature generous and possessed of great moral resolve.

sentences.zh: 書為當時第一，畫亦入妙品。

translations.literal: His calligraphy was first in the age; his painting also entered the sublime grade.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy ranked first in his day, and his painting reached the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 評者謂畫高於書，書高於詩，詩高於文，然王庭筠獨以其才具許之。

translations.literal: Critics said painting was higher than calligraphy, calligraphy higher than poetry, poetry higher than prose—yet Wang Tingyun alone praised him for his endowment of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that his painting surpassed his calligraphy, his calligraphy his poetry, and his poetry his prose—yet Wang Tingyun alone praised the breadth of his gifts.

sentences.zh: 登正隆二年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenglong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenglong.

sentences.zh: 曆益都都勾判官，北京鹽使。

translations.literal: He served as Yidu metropolitan investigating administrative aide and Beijing salt commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigating administrative aide of Yidu and as Beijing salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 年六十四致仕，優遊鄉里，家藏法書名畫數百軸。

translations.literal: At age sixty-four he retired; he wandered at ease in his home district, his household storing several hundred scrolls of model calligraphy and famous paintings.
translations.idiomatic: He retired at sixty-four and lived at ease in his home district, keeping several hundred scrolls of master calligraphy and famous paintings.

sentences.zh: 年七十卒。

translations.literal: At age seventy he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 趙可，字獻之，高平人。

translations.literal: Zhao Ke, style name Xianzhi, was a native of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ke, whose style name was Xianzhi, came from Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi graduate in the second year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 仕至翰林直學士。

translations.literal: He served up to Hanlin Direct Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Hanlin direct academician.

sentences.zh: 博學高才，卓犖不羈。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with lofty talent, outstanding and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned, brilliantly gifted, and unconstrained by convention.

sentences.zh: 天德、貞元間，有聲場屋。

translations.literal: Between Tiande and Zhenyuan he had renown in the examination halls.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Tiande and Zhenyuan eras he was famed in the examination halls.

sentences.zh: 後入翰林，一時詔誥多出其手，流輩服其典雅。

translations.literal: Later he entered the Hanlin; for a time most edicts and rescripts came from his hand, and his peers submitted to his elegance.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the Hanlin Academy, most court edicts and rescripts of the day came from his hand, and his contemporaries admired his refined style.

sentences.zh: 其歌詩樂府尤工，號《玉峰散人集》。

translations.literal: His songs, poetry, and yuefu were especially skilled; they were titled "Collected Works of the Jade-Peak Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: His songs, poetry, and yuefu were especially accomplished, collected under the title "Works of the Jade-Peak Recluse."

sentences.zh: 郭長倩

translations.literal: Guo Changqian.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Changqian.

sentences.zh: 郭長倩，字曼卿，文登人。

translations.literal: Guo Changqian, style name Manqing, was a native of Wendeng.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Changqian, whose style name was Manqing, came from Wendeng.

sentences.zh: 登皇統丙寅經義乙科。

translations.literal: He passed the Huangtong bingyin Classics Meaning examination, second class.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Classics Meaning examination in the bingyin year of Huangtong, second class.

sentences.zh: 仕至秘書少監，兼禮部郎中，修起居注。

translations.literal: He served up to Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Director of the Ministry of Rites, compiling the Diurnal Record.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Secretariat, concurrently director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 與施朋望、王無競、劉岩老、劉無党相友善。

translations.literal: With Shi Pengwang, Wang Wujing, Liu Yanlao, and Liu Wudang he was mutually friendly.
translations.idiomatic: He was on close terms with Shi Pengwang, Wang Wujing, Liu Yanlao, and Liu Wudang.

sentences.zh: 所撰《石決明傳》為時輩所稱。

translations.literal: His composition "Biography of Stone Cassia" was praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: His "Biography of Stone Cassia" was praised by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 有《昆侖集》行於世。

translations.literal: He had "Kunlun Collection" circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His "Kunlun Collection" circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 蕭永祺

translations.literal: Xiao Yongqi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yongqi.

sentences.zh: 蕭永祺，字景純，本名蒲烈。

translations.literal: Xiao Yongqi, style name Jingchun, original name Pulie.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yongqi, whose style name was Jingchun and whose original name was Pulie,

sentences.zh: 少好學，通契丹大小字。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and mastered the large and small Khitan scripts.
translations.idiomatic: loved learning from youth and mastered both the large and small Khitan scripts.

sentences.zh: 廣甯尹耶律固奉詔譯書，時置門下，因盡傳其業。

translations.literal: Guangning Prefect Yelü Gu received the edict to translate books; at the time he was placed at the gate, and thereby fully transmitted his craft.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangning prefect Yelü Gu was ordered to translate books, Yongqi was placed in his household and received his full instruction.

sentences.zh: 固卒，永祺率門弟子服齊衰喪。

translations.literal: When Gu died, Yongqi led the gate's disciples in wearing one-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu died, Yongqi led his fellow disciples in wearing one-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 固作《遼史》未成，永祺繼之，作紀三十卷、志五卷、傳四十卷，上之。

translations.literal: Gu composed the "History of Liao" but did not finish it; Yongqi continued it, composing thirty chapters of annals, five of treatises, and forty of biographies, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had left the "History of Liao" unfinished; Yongqi continued it, completing thirty chapters of annals, five of treatises, and forty of biographies, and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 加宣武將軍，除太常丞。

translations.literal: He was added General of Manifest Martiality and appointed Vice Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and appointed vice director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 海陵為中京留守，永祺特見親禮。

translations.literal: When Hailing was garrison commander of the Central Capital, Yongqi was especially shown intimate courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing served as garrison commander of the Central Capital, Yongqi received his special favor.

sentences.zh: 天德初，擢左諫議大夫，遷翰林侍講學士，同修國史，再遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was promoted Left Remonstrance Censor, transferred to Hanlin Attendant Lecturer, concurrently revised the national history, and again transferred to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiande era he was promoted to left remonstrance censor, then to Hanlin attendant lecturer and compiler of the national history, and again to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷承旨。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Hanlin academician expositor.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞耶律安禮出守南京，海陵欲以永祺代之，召見於內閣，諭以旨意，永祺辭曰：「臣才識卑下，不足以辱執政。」

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Yelü Anli went out to guard Nanjing; Hailing wished to replace him with Yongqi, summoned him to audience in the inner pavilion, and instructed him of the intent; Yongqi declined, saying: "Your servant's talent and knowledge are low and mean—not sufficient to disgrace the handling of government."
translations.idiomatic: When left vice director Yelü Anli was sent to guard Nanjing, Hailing wished to replace him with Yongqi and summoned him to the inner pavilion to explain his intent; Yongqi declined, saying, "My talent and learning are too slight to bear the burden of high office."

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「今天下無事，朕方以文治，卿為是優矣。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "Now the realm is without affairs; I am just then employing literary governance—you are superior in this."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "The realm is at peace, and I am pursuing civil governance—you are well suited to it."

sentences.zh: 永祺固辭。

translations.literal: Yongqi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqi still refused.

sentences.zh: 既出，或問曰：「公遇知人主，進取爵位，以道佐時，何多讓也？」

translations.literal: After he came out, someone asked: "Sir, meeting a ruler who knows men, advancing to rank and title, assisting the age with the Way—why so much yielding?"
translations.idiomatic: After he left, someone asked, "You have met a ruler who knows talent and could advance in rank to aid the age—why refuse so much?"

sentences.zh: 永祺曰：「執政系天下休戚，縱欲貪冒榮寵，如蒼生何！」

translations.literal: Yongqi said: "Holding government binds the realm's weal and woe; even if one wished to covet glory and favor greedily—what of the common people!"
translations.idiomatic: Yongqi replied, "High office bears on the welfare of the realm; even if one craved rank and favor, what would become of the people?"

sentences.zh: 海陵嘗選廷臣十人備諮訪，獨永祺議論寬厚，時稱長者。

translations.literal: Hailing once selected ten court ministers to prepare for consultation; Yongqi alone in discussion was generous and thick—his age called him a man of mature virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing once chose ten court ministers for consultation, Yongqi alone was noted for his generous and measured discourse, and contemporaries called him a man of true magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十七。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 胡礪，字元化，磁州武安人。

translations.literal: Hu Li, style name Yuanhua, was a native of Wu'an in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Li, whose style name was Yuanhua, came from Wu'an in Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 少嗜學。

translations.literal: From youth he was addicted to learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was devoted to study.

sentences.zh: 天會間，大軍下河北，礪為軍士所掠，行至燕，亡匿香山寺，與傭保雜處。

translations.literal: During Tianhui the great army descended on Hebei; Li was plundered by soldiers; traveling to Yan he hid in Xiangshan Temple, mingling with hired laborers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhui era, when the main army swept through Hebei, Li was seized by soldiers; he fled to Yan and hid in Xiangshan Temple, living among hired laborers.

sentences.zh: 韓昉見而異之，使賦詩以見志，礪操筆立成，思致清婉，昉喜甚，因館置門下，使與其子處，同教育之，自是學業日進。

translations.literal: Han Fang saw him and regarded him as extraordinary, had him compose a poem to show his intent; Li took up the brush and finished at once, thought and expression clear and gentle; Fang was greatly pleased, and therefore lodged him at his gate, had him dwell with his sons, jointly educating him—from then his studies daily advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fang noticed him, asked him to write a poem expressing his aspirations, and Li composed one immediately with clear and graceful thought; Fang was delighted, took him into his household, and had him study with his sons, after which Li's learning advanced daily.

sentences.zh: 昉嘗謂人曰：「胡生才器一日千里，他日必將名世。」

translations.literal: Fang once said to people: "Master Hu's talent and capacity advance a thousand li in a day; another day he will certainly make his name in the world."
translations.idiomatic: Fang once said, "Master Hu's talent advances a thousand li in a day; he will surely make his name in the world."

sentences.zh: 十年，舉進士第一，授右拾遺，權翰林修撰。

translations.literal: Ten years later he was nominated first in the jinshi examination, appointed Right Reminder, and provisionally Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later he took first place in the jinshi examination and was appointed right reminder and acting Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 久之，改定州觀察判官。

translations.literal: After a long time he was changed to Dingzhou observation administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made administrative aide to the Dingzhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 定之學校為河朔冠，士子聚居者常以百數，礪督教不倦，經指授者悉為場屋上游，稱其程文為「元化格」。

translations.literal: Ding's schools were the crown of Hebei; scholars gathering to dwell there were often in the hundreds; Li supervised instruction without weariness; those who received his guidance all became top rank in the examination halls—his examination essays were called the "Yuanhua style."
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou's schools were the finest in Hebei, with hundreds of students in residence; Li taught tirelessly, and those he instructed regularly ranked at the top in examinations—his model essays were called the "Yuanhua style."

sentences.zh: 皇統初，為河北西路轉運都勾判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong he was Hedong West Circuit transport investigating administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Huangtong he became investigating administrative aide on the Hebei West transport commission.

sentences.zh: 礪性剛直無所屈。

translations.literal: Li's nature was upright and firm, yielding to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Li was by nature upright and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 行台平章政事高楨之汴，道真定，燕于漕司。

translations.literal: Branch Secretariat Grand Councilor Gao Zhen went to Bian, passed through Zhending, and feasted at the transport office.
translations.idiomatic: Branch secretariat grand councilor Gao Zhen traveled to Bianjing, passed through Zhending, and was entertained at the transport commission.

sentences.zh: 礪欲就坐，楨責之，礪曰：「公在政府則禮絕百僚，今日之會自有賓主禮。」

translations.literal: Li wished to take his seat; Zhen reproached him; Li said: "Sir, in the government the rites cut off all officials—but today's gathering has its own guest-and-host rites."
translations.idiomatic: When Li was about to take his seat, Zhen rebuked him; Li replied, "In the central government your rank sets you apart from all officials, but at today's gathering the rites of host and guest still apply."

sentences.zh: 楨曰：「汝他日為省吏當何如？」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "You, another day as a secretariat clerk—how ought you act?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "If you become a secretariat clerk one day, how will you behave then?"

sentences.zh: 礪曰：「當官而行，亦何所避。」

translations.literal: Li said: "When holding office one acts accordingly—what is there to avoid?"
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "One acts as office requires—what is there to shrink from?"

sentences.zh: 楨壯其言，改謝之。

translations.literal: Zhen admired his words and changed to apologize to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen admired his reply and apologized to him.

sentences.zh: 改同知深州軍州事，加朝奉大夫。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Commissioner of Shenzhou military and civil affairs, added Gentleman for Court Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of Shenzhou and given the rank of Gentleman for Court Attendance.

sentences.zh: 郡守暴戾，蔑視僚屬，礪常以禮折之，守愧服，郡事一委於礪。

translations.literal: The prefect was violent and cruel, despising subordinate officials; Li often used rites to check him; the prefect felt ashamed and submitted; prefectural affairs were entirely entrusted to Li.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was brutal and despised his staff; Li regularly checked him with proper ceremony until the prefect submitted in shame and entrusted all prefectural affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 州管五縣，例置弓手百餘，少者猶六七十人，歲征民錢五千余萬為顧直。

translations.literal: The prefecture governed five counties; by precedent more than a hundred bowmen were established, fewer still sixty or seventy; yearly levying from the people more than fifty million in cash as guard pay.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture administered five counties and by custom maintained more than a hundred bowmen, or at least sixty or seventy, levying more than fifty million in cash annually from the people as guard pay.

sentences.zh: 其人皆市井無賴，以跡盜為名，所至擾民。

translations.literal: These men were all marketplace ruffians, taking the name of tracking thieves—wherever they went they disturbed the people.
translations.idiomatic: They were market riffraff who went about under the name of thief-catchers and harassed the people wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 礪知其弊，悉罷去。

translations.literal: Li knew their abuses and entirely dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: Li saw the abuse and abolished them entirely.

sentences.zh: 繼而有飛語曰：「某日賊發，將殺通守。」

translations.literal: Then there was a flying rumor saying: "On a certain day bandits will rise and kill the administrative commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Soon a rumor spread: "On a certain day bandits would rise and kill the administrative commissioner."

sentences.zh: 或請為備，礪曰：「盜所利者財耳，吾貧如此，何備為。」

translations.literal: Someone requested preparations; Li said: "Thieves profit only in wealth—I am poor like this; what preparations are needed?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged precautions, Li said, "Thieves want only wealth, and I am as poor as this—what need is there for precautions?"

sentences.zh: 是夕，令公署撤關，竟亦無事。

translations.literal: That evening he ordered the government offices to remove the barriers; in the end there was also no incident.
translations.idiomatic: That night he ordered the government offices to leave their gates unbarred, and nothing happened.

sentences.zh: 再補翰林修撰，遷禮部郎中，一時典禮多所裁定。

translations.literal: Again appointed Hanlin Compiler, transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites; for a time many ritual codes were decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Hanlin compiler and promoted to director of the Ministry of Rites, determining many ritual questions of the day.

sentences.zh: 海陵拜平章政事，百官賀於廟堂，礪獨不跪。

translations.literal: When Hailing was invested Grand Councilor, the hundred officials congratulated in the temple hall; Li alone did not kneel.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was appointed grand councilor, the officials offered congratulations in the temple hall, but Li alone did not kneel.

sentences.zh: 海陵問其故，礪以令對，且曰：「朝服而跪，見君父禮也。」

translations.literal: Hailing asked the reason; Li answered according to regulations and said: "In court dress to kneel is the rite of seeing ruler and father."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing asked why; Li cited the regulations and said, "Kneeling in court dress is the rite owed to the ruler and father."

sentences.zh: 海陵深器重之。

translations.literal: Hailing deeply valued and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 天德初，再遷侍講學士，同修國史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was again transferred to Attendant Lecturer and concurrently revised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiande era he was again promoted to attendant lecturer and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去官。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his mother he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 起複為宋國歲元副使，刑部侍郎白彥恭為使，海陵謂礪曰：「彥恭官在卿下，以其舊勞，故使卿副之。」

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning as vice envoy for Song's New Year, with Ministry of Punishments Vice Director Bai Yangong as envoy; Hailing said to Li: "Yangong's office is below yours, but because of his old merit I therefore have you serve as deputy."
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as vice envoy for the Song New Year mission, with Bai Yangong of the Ministry of Punishments as chief envoy; Hailing told Li, "Yangong's rank is below yours, but because of his long service I have made you his deputy."

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician and changed to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician and then minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 扈從至汴得疾，海陵數遣使臨問，卒，深悼惜之。

translations.literal: Accompanying the entourage to Bian he fell ill; Hailing repeatedly sent envoys to visit and inquire; he died, and Hailing deeply mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill while accompanying the court to Bianjing; Hailing sent envoys repeatedly to inquire after him; when he died, Hailing mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 年五十五。

translations.literal: His age was fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 王競，字無競，彰德人。

translations.literal: Wang Jing, style name Wujing, was a native of Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing, whose style name was Wujing, came from Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 警敏好學。

translations.literal: Alert and keen, he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 年十七以廕補官。

translations.literal: At age seventeen he entered office by yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he entered office through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 宋宣和中，太學兩試合格，調屯留主簿。

translations.literal: During Song Xuanhe he twice passed the Imperial Academy examinations and was assigned registrar of Tunliu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanhe reign he twice passed the Imperial Academy examinations and was appointed registrar of Tunliu.

sentences.zh: 入國朝，除大寧令，曆寶勝鹽官，轉河內令。

translations.literal: Entering the dynasty, he was appointed magistrate of Daning, served as Baosheng salt official, and transferred to magistrate of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Jin service he was made magistrate of Daning, served as salt commissioner of Baosheng, and was transferred to magistrate of Henei.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑盜起，競設方略以購賊，不數月盡得之。

translations.literal: At that time the year was famine-stricken and bandits arose; Jing devised plans to offer rewards for capturing thieves, and within a few months obtained them all.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine bandits rose; Jing devised a reward scheme for their capture, and within a few months had seized them all.

sentences.zh: 夏秋之交，沁水泛溢，歲發民築堤，豪民猾吏因緣為奸，競核實之，減費幾半，縣民為之諺曰：「西山至河岸，縣官兩人半。」

translations.literal: Between summer and autumn the Qin River overflowed; yearly the people were mobilized to build dikes; powerful locals and crafty clerks seized opportunities for corruption; Jing verified the accounts, reducing costs by nearly half; the county people made a proverb saying: "From West Mountain to the riverbank, the county officials are two and a half men."
translations.idiomatic: Between summer and autumn the Qin River flooded, and each year the people were conscripted to build dikes while powerful locals and corrupt clerks profited; Jing audited the accounts and cut costs nearly in half, and the people coined a saying: "From West Mountain to the riverbank—the county has two and a half officials."

sentences.zh: 蓋以前政韓希甫與競相繼治縣，皆有幹能，絳州正平令張元亦有治績而差不及，故雲然。

translations.literal: This was because the previous administrator Han Xifu and Jing in succession governed the county, all possessing ability; Jiangzhou Zhengping magistrate Zhang Yuan also had governing achievements but was somewhat inferior—thus it was said so.
translations.idiomatic: This referred to the successive administrations of Han Xifu and Jing, both men of real ability, and to Zhang Yuan, magistrate of Zhengping in Jiangzhou, whose achievements fell somewhat short—hence the saying.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，轉固安令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan he was transferred to magistrate of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjuan he was transferred to magistrate of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，參政韓昉薦之，召權應奉翰林文字，兼太常博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong Vice Grand Councilor Han Fang recommended him; he was summoned provisionally as Attendant for Hanlin Documents and concurrently Grand Master of Ceremonies academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Huangtong, vice grand councilor Han Fang recommended him; he was summoned as acting attendant for Hanlin documents and concurrently academician of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 詔作《金源郡王完顏婁室墓碑》，競以行狀盡其實，乃請國史刑正之，時人以為法。

translations.literal: An edict ordered composition of the "Stele Inscription for Prince of Jinyuan Commandery Wanyan Loushi"; Jing used the conduct narrative to exhaust the facts, then requested the national history office to correct and revise it—contemporaries took this as a model.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compose the stele inscription for Prince Wanyan Loushi of Jinyuan; Jing drew on the conduct narrative to state the facts fully and asked the historiographical office to revise it—contemporaries took this as the proper method.

sentences.zh: 二年，試館閣，競文居最，遂為真。

translations.literal: In the second year he was tested at the Hall and Pavilion; Jing's writing ranked first, and he then became permanent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he passed the Hanlin examination with the highest-ranked essay and received a permanent appointment.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時海陵當國，政由己出，欲令百官避堂諱，競言人臣無公諱，遂止。

translations.literal: At that time Hailing held state power, government proceeding from himself; he wished to have the hundred officials avoid hall taboos; Jing said ministers had no public taboo—and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing held power and wished to require officials to avoid his personal taboo, Jing argued that ministers owed no such public taboo, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 蕭仲恭乙太傅領三省事封王，欲援遼故事，親王用紫羅傘。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhonggong was appointed Grand Mentor leading the Three Departments affairs and enfeoffed as prince; he wished to cite Liao precedent—that imperial princes use purple silk umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Zhonggong was appointed grand mentor, placed in charge of the Three Departments, and enfeoffed as prince, he sought to follow Liao precedent and use a purple silk umbrella reserved for imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 事下禮部，競與郎中翟永固明言其非是，事竟不行，海陵由是重之。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Ministry of Rites; Jing together with Director Zhai Yonggu clearly stated its incorrectness; the matter in the end was not carried out; Hailing thereby valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites; Jing and director Zhai Yonggu plainly declared it improper, and the proposal was abandoned; Hailing thereafter held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 天德初，轉翰林待制，遷翰林直學士，改禮部侍郎，遷翰林侍講學士，改太常卿，同修國史，擢禮部尚書，同修國史如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was transferred to Hanlin Awaiting Draftsman, promoted to Hanlin Direct Academician, changed to Vice Minister of Rites, transferred to Hanlin Attendant Lecturer, changed to Grand Master of Ceremonies, concurrently revised the national history, promoted to Minister of Rites, revising national history as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tiande he rose through Hanlin awaiting draftsman and direct academician to vice minister of rites, Hanlin attendant lecturer, grand master of ceremonies, and minister of rites, while continuing to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 大定二年春，從太傅張浩朝京師，詔複為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Dading he followed Grand Mentor Zhang Hao in audience at the capital; an edict restored him as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Dading he accompanied grand mentor Zhang Hao to the capital and was by edict restored as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 是歲，奉遷睿宗山陵，儀注不應典禮，競削官兩階。

translations.literal: That year, in conducting the transfer of Ruizong's mountain tomb, the ritual regulations did not accord with canonical rites; Jing was reduced two ranks in office.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the removal of Ruizong's tomb to the mountain mausoleum, the ceremonial regulations failed to meet canonical standards, and Jing was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 詔改創五龍車，兼翰林學士承旨，修國史。

translations.literal: An edict ordered redesign of the Five-Dragon carriage; he concurrently served as Hanlin Academician Expositor and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he redesigned the Five-Dragon carriage, served as Hanlin academician expositor, and compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 競博學而能文，善草隸書，工大字，兩都宮殿榜題，皆競所書，士林推為第一雲。

translations.literal: Jing was broadly learned and able in prose, skilled in cursive and clerical script, accomplished in large characters; the two capitals' palace hall inscriptions were all written by Jing—the scholarly grove praised him as first, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was broadly learned and accomplished in prose, skilled in cursive and clerical script and especially in large characters; the inscription plaques of the palaces in both capitals were all his work, and scholars ranked him first.

sentences.zh: 楊伯仁

translations.literal: Yang Boren.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Boren.

sentences.zh: 楊伯仁，字安道，伯雄之弟也。

translations.literal: Yang Boren, style name Andao, was Borexiong's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Boren, whose style name was Andao, was the younger brother of Yang Boxiong.

sentences.zh: 天性孝友，讀書一過成誦。

translations.literal: By nature filial and friendly, in reading a book once he could recite it.
translations.idiomatic: By nature filial and devoted to his brothers, he could recite a text after reading it once.

sentences.zh: 登皇統九年進士第，事親不求調。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Huangtong; in serving his parents he did not seek appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Huangtong and declined appointment in order to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，除應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was appointed Attendant for Hanlin Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande he was appointed attendant for Hanlin documents.

sentences.zh: 初名伯英，避太子光英諱，改今名。

translations.literal: His original name was Boying; to avoid Crown Prince Guangying's taboo he changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Boying; to avoid the taboo of Crown Prince Guangying he adopted his present name.

sentences.zh: 海陵嘗夜召賦詩，傳趣甚亟，未二鼓奏十詠，海陵喜，解衣賜之。

translations.literal: Hailing once summoned him at night to compose poetry; the messenger's urging was very urgent; before the second watch he presented ten pieces; Hailing was pleased and bestowed his own robe.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing once summoned him at night to compose poetry with urgent dispatch; before the second watch he presented ten poems, and Hailing was so pleased that he gave him his own robe.

sentences.zh: 海陵射烏，伯仁獻《獲烏詩》以諷。

translations.literal: Hailing shot crows; Boren presented "Poem on Obtaining Crows" to admonish indirectly.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing went crow-shooting, Boren presented a "Poem on Capturing Crows" as indirect admonition.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複，賜金帶襲衣，及賜白金以奉母。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his father he was recalled; he was bestowed a gold belt and court robe, and also bestowed white gold to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was recalled and granted a gold belt, court robe, and white gold to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 改左拾遺。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left reminder.

sentences.zh: 進士呂忠翰廷試已在第一，未唱名，海陵以忠翰程文示伯仁，問其優劣，伯仁對曰：「當在優等。」

translations.literal: Jinshi Lü Zhonghan in the palace examination was already first, the names not yet announced; Hailing showed Zhonghan's examination essay to Boren and asked its relative merit; Boren replied: "It ought to be in the superior grade."
translations.idiomatic: The jinshi Lü Zhonghan had already ranked first in the palace examination before the names were announced; Hailing showed Boren his essay and asked its merit; Boren replied, "It belongs in the highest grade."

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「此今試狀元也。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "This is today's examination top graduate."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "This is today's top examination graduate."

sentences.zh: 伯仁自以知忠翰姓名在第一，遂宿諫省，俟唱名乃出，海陵嘉其慎密。

translations.literal: Boren himself knew Zhonghan's name was first; he therefore lodged in the remonstrance office, waiting until the names were announced before coming out; Hailing praised his caution and discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Zhonghan was first, Boren stayed overnight in the remonstrance office and did not emerge until the names were announced; Hailing praised his discretion.

sentences.zh: 轉翰林修撰。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 孟宗獻發解第一，伯仁讀其程文，稱之「此人當成大名」。

translations.literal: Meng Zongxian ranked first in the qualifying examination; Boren read his examination essay and praised him: "This man will certainly achieve a great name."
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zongxian took first place in the qualifying examination, Boren read his essay and said, "This man will surely make a great name."

sentences.zh: 是歲，宗獻府試、省試、廷試皆第一，號「孟四元」，時論以為知文。
